hypothesis: If the claim holds, mean stature velocity by age will be highest in infancy, fall to a low steady rate in mid-childhood, rise again in the early teens, and approach zero in adulthood.
pass_criterion: From mean measured stature by single year of age, velocity at age 0-1 exceeds that at age 5-8; velocity at the pubertal peak (age 10-15) is at least 20% greater than the minimum between ages 5-9; velocity at age >= 19 is < 1 cm/yr.
fail_criterion: No pubertal rise (peak velocity at age 10-15 is < 5% above the 5-9 minimum), or velocity is not highest in infancy.
interpretation: 'Curve of growth' is taken as the age-specific mean of measured stature, from which velocity is estimated by differencing. Cross-sectional means approximate the longitudinal curve. 'Growing age' means the pubertal spurt.
